# Entropy generated by cooling a finite body in a reservoir

↑ **Parent:** [Entropy](entropy-split.md)

For a body of constant [heat capacity](heat-capacity.md) $C$ cooling from $T_i$ to a [thermal reservoir](heat-bath.md) at $T_0>0$, the body's [entropy](entropy-split.md) change is $C\ln(T_0/T_i)$, while the reservoir gains $C(T_i-T_0)/T_0$. Their sum is nonnegative because $r-1-\ln r\geq0$ for $r=T_i/T_0>0$. The logarithmic body contribution is computed along a hypothetical reversible path; the actual finite-temperature-difference heat transfer is irreversible.
